message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, so I can’t give you the current temperature or forecast.  
If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, San Francisco usually has mild, temperate weather year‑round—average highs in the 60–70 °F (15–21 °C) range and relatively low humidity. For the exact current conditions, you might want to check a weather app or website like Weather.com, AccuWeather, or the National Weather Service.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the weather in San francisco?" We need to provide weather info. We have no direct API to fetch weather. We can either say we don't have real-time data or we can use a placeholder. The user didn't specify a date. We can respond with a general statement: "I don't have real-time data." Or we can ask for clarification. According to policy, we should not hallucinate. So we should say we don't have real-time data. We can offer to provide typical weather patterns. So answer: "I don't have real-time data, but typical weather in SF is mild, etc."
